The *Kusumāsaniyattheraapadāna* is a verse narrative preserved within the Therāpadāna collection of the Pali Canon [SuttaCentral]. Representing the biographical reminiscences of the elder Kusumāsaniya, it belongs to the late canonical stratum of biographical poems concerning the past deeds and spiritual attainments of Buddhist elders. SuttaCentral records five modern translations of the text in five languages [SuttaCentral].
No direct external parallels in Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan corpora are recorded [DharmaNexus]. Internally, DharmaNexus identifies 39 matching passages shared across 14 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The most substantial reuse occurs in the commentary to the Theragāthā (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, first part), which shares nine passages (1,383 characters), with segments §0.3–9.4 showing high alignment (similarity 0.93) to the commentary's narrative context [DharmaNexus]. In addition, stock verses from segments §8–11 are shared with multiple other poems in the Therāpadāna, most prominently *Pāyasadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 125), *Kilañjadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 236), *Ñāṇasaññikattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 130), and *Tālavaṇṭadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 219) [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
